{{Short description|Mathematical observation}}
{{notability|date=March 2023}}
In [[topology]], a branch of mathematics, and specifically [[knot theory]], the '''lamp cord trick''' is an observation that two certain spaces are [[homeomorphic]], even if one of the components is knotted.  The spaces are <math>M^3\backslash T_i,i=1,2</math>, where <math>M^3</math> is a hollow ball homeomorphic to <math>S^2\times[0,1]</math> and <math>T_i</math> a tube connecting the boundary components of <math>M^3</math>.  The name comes from R. H. Bing's book "The Geometric Topology of 3-manifolds".<ref>{{cite book | url=https://books.google.com/books?id=TASWAwAAQBAJ | title=The Geometric Topology of 3-manifolds | isbn=9780821810408 | last1=Bing | first1=R. H. | date=31 December 1983 }}</ref>
